chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Jundab, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan Al-Mazi (peace be upon him be peace (about) what I should say in the prostration of gratitude, for our companions differed regarding it, so he (peace be upon him) said: Say while you are prostrating.

O Allah, I bear witness to You, and I bear witness to Your angels, and Your prophets, and Your messengers, and all of Your creation, that You are Allah my Lord, and Islam is my religion, and Muhammad is my prophet, and Ali, and so-and-so, and so-and-so, up to the last of them, are my Imams. With them I befriend and from their enemies I disavow.

O Allah, I adjure You by the blood of the oppressed (three times). O Allah, I adjure You by Your promise upon Yourself regarding Your guardians, that You make them victorious over Your enemy and their enemy, that You send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the protected ones from the family of Muhammad. O Allah, I ask You for ease after difficulty (three times).

Then place your right cheek on the ground and say: O my refuge, when the paths weary me and the earth is straitened for me despite its vastness, and O Creator of my creation, have mercy on me, although You were needless of my creation. Send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the protected ones from the family of Muhammad.
Then place your left cheek (on the ground) and say: O Humiliator of every tyrant, and O Honorer of every humbled one. And I swear by Your Might that my striving has reached its end (three times).
Then say: O Affectionate, O Bestower, O Remover of great distress (three times).
Then return to prostration and say one hundred times: Thank You, Thank You. Then ask for your need, if Allah, the Exalted, wills.
ai.seo_question: What are the specific words and actions for the prostration of gratitude in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) prescribes a comprehensive supplication for Sajdat al-Shukr that integrates theological affirmation with political loyalty to the Imams. It uniquely emphasizes the concept of 'anshodu' (adjuring) by the blood of the oppressed, reflecting the Shia tradition of connecting gratitude to divine justice and the eventual triumph of the Ahl al-Bayt. The ritual concludes with repeated expressions of thanks, highlighting the spiritual discipline of maintaining gratitude even amidst worldly trials.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Jundab who said,

‘I asked Abu Al-Hassan Al-Maazyasws (7th Imamasws) about what I should be saying during a Sajdah of gratitude, for our companions have differed with regards to it’. So heasws said: ‘Say while you are in Sajdah,

‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! I keep You<sup>azwj</sup> as a Witness, and keep as a witness Your<sup>azwj</sup> Angels, and Your<sup>azwj</sup> Prophets<sup>as</sup>, and Your<sup>azwj</sup> Mursil Prophets<sup>as</sup>, and the entirety of Your<sup>azwj</sup> creature that You<sup>azwj</sup> are Allah<sup>azwj</sup> my Lord<sup>azwj</sup>, and Al-Islam is my Religion, and Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> is my Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, and Ali<sup>asws</sup> and so and so, up to the last of them<sup>asws</sup>, they<sup>asws</sup> are my Imams<sup>asws</sup>. With them<sup>asws</sup> I befriend and from their<sup>asws</sup> enemies I disavow.

O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! I adjure You<sup>azwj</sup> by the blood of the oppressed’ (Imam Husayn<sup>asws</sup>) – three times. O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! I adjure You<sup>azwj</sup> with Your<sup>azwj</sup> Promise upon Yourself<sup>azwj</sup> of Making Your<sup>azwj</sup> Guardians<sup>asws</sup> victorious upon Your<sup>azwj</sup> enemies and their<sup>asws</sup> enemies, that You<sup>azwj</sup> Send Blessings upon Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> and the upon the weak ones from the Progeny<sup>asws</sup> of Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>. O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! I ask You<sup>azwj</sup> for the ease after the difficulties’ – three times.

Then place your right cheek upon the ground and you should be saying, ‘O my Cave where the doctrines wear me down and the earth is straitened upon me with what I wish for, and O Initiator of my creation, be Merciful with me, and You<sup>azwj</sup> were needless of my creation, Send Blessings upon Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> and upon the weak ones from the Progeny<sup>asws</sup> of Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>’.

Then place your left cheek (upon the ground) and you should be saying, 
;O Humiliator of every tyrant, and O Honourer of every humiliated one. And I swear by Your<sup>azwj</sup> Might that my striving has reached its end’ – three times.
Then you should be saying, ‘O Affectionate, O Bestower, O Remover of the great worries! – three times.
Then return to the Sajdah, and you should be saying one hundred times, ‘Thank Youazwj! Thank Youazwj!’ Then you should ask for your need, Allahazwj Willing’.
en.sarwar: 17. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ‘Abd Allah ibn Jundab who has said the following: “I asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about what to say in prostration for thanksgiving because our people are not of the same idea about it.

He told me to say the following in a prostrating position: ‘O Lord, I beg You to bear witness, I beg Your angels, Your prophets, messengers and all of Your creatures to bear witness (to my testimony) that You are Allah. You are my Lord. Islam is my religion and Muhammad is my prophet. Ali and all of my ’A’immah so and so’ - mentioning one by one - ‘al- Hassan, al-Husayn, Ali ibn al-Husayn, Muhammad ibn Ali, Ja‘far ibn Muhammad, Musa ibn Ja‘far, Ali ibn Musa, Muhammad ibn Ali, Ali ibn Muhammad, al-Hassan ibn Ali and al-Mahdi are my ’A’immah, ‘Alayhim al-Salam. I have acknowledged their divine authority and as my guardians, I love them and I denounce their enemies.

O Lord, I plead before You through the blood of the one who suffered injustice,’ - three times - ‘O Lord I plead before You through Your firm undertaking of granting victory to Your friends - those whom You have entrusted with Your Authority- over Your enemy as well as their enemy. O Allah, I appeal before You to grant Muhammad and those members of his family who have safeguarded their trust compensation. Grant them a compensation worthy of their services to Your cause. O Lord, I request You to grant me comfort after suffering’ - three times.

Then place the right side of your face on the ground. Say, ‘O my protector at times when all means become useless and the whole wide world seems to have become narrow, O my creator due to His mercy not because of being in need of such creation, O Allah, grant proper compensation to Muhammad and those members of his family who have safeguarded their trust.’
Then place the left side of your face on the ground and say, ‘O subjugator of tyrants and bestowing honor to the oppressed ones. I swear by Your majesty that my efforts are exhausted’ - three times.
Then say, ‘O the affectionate one, the One who grants favors, O the One who removes great hardships’ - three times.
Then bow down for prostration and say one hundred times, ‘Shukran’ (I thank You, O Lord); then ask from Allah what you need by the will of Allah, the most High.’”
